questions.statement: Which sentence describes a morning routine correctly?

options.text: She get up at six and eat breakfast.
options.feedback: Both verbs need the -s of the third person singular.

options.text: She is get up at six and eat breakfast.
options.feedback: The present continuous does not describe a daily habit.

options.text: She get up at six and is eat breakfast.
options.feedback: Mixing two present forms leaves the sentence ungrammatical.

options.text: She gets up at six and eats breakfast.
options.feedback: 'Gets up' shows the third person singular of the routine.

questions.explanation:
Las rutinas se expresan en presente simple con la tercera persona singular terminada en -s.

questions.statement: What does the expression 'get dressed' mean?

options.feedback: 'Get dressed' is the fixed expression for putting on clothes.
That would be 'clean your room'.
That would be 'brush your teeth'.
That would be 'make the bed'.

questions.explanation:
'Get dressed' significa ponerse la ropa, una accion habitual de la manana. El mismo criterio se aplica al resto del vocabulario del tema.

questions.statement: Complete: 'After school I ____ my homework and then I play.'

options.feedback: 'Does' is the third person singular form and does not agree with 'I'.
'Am doing' would be present continuous, a different tense.
'Do my homework' is the standard expression with the base form after 'I'.
A gerund alone cannot act as the verb of the clause.

questions.explanation:
La segunda parte usa el presente simple con 'I', por lo que el verbo va en forma base.

questions.statement: Choose the word that means 'to go to bed'.

options.feedback: 'Go to school' refers to attending lessons.
'Go to bed' is the standard expression for going to sleep.
'Go to work' refers to an adult job.
'Go home' returns to one's house, not necessarily to sleep.

questions.explanation:
'Go to bed' es la expresion fija para acostarse. Esta estructura se repite con otros sustantivos del mismo grupo.

questions.statement: Look at the text: 'Carlos brushes his teeth, washes his face and goes to school.' What is the main idea?

options.text: It describes how to brush teeth.
options.feedback: Only one action is detailed; the text covers the whole routine.

options.text: It explains why school is important.
options.feedback: The text never states a reason or opinion about school.
All three actions belong to a morning routine.

options.text: It compares Carlos with another student.
options.feedback: No other student appears in the text.

questions.explanation:
Las tres acciones descritas forman parte de la rutina matutina de Carlos. La regla se aprende junto con los demas ejemplos de la unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the present simple correctly with a plural subject?

options.text: My friends plays football on Sundays.
options.feedback: The -s would be required only for he, she or it.

options.text: My friends play football on Sundays.
options.feedback: 'Friends' is plural, so the base form 'play' is correct.

options.text: My friends is play football on Sundays.
options.feedback: The singular auxiliary 'is' contradicts the plural subject.

options.text: My friends are play football on Sundays.
options.feedback: 'Are' plus the bare verb 'play' is not a valid combination.

questions.explanation:
Un sujeto plural no lleva -s en el presente simple; el verbo aparece en forma base. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the best time expression for a habit: 'She ____ coffee every morning.'

options.feedback: 'Every morning' marks a habit, so the present simple 'drinks' is required.
The present continuous would suggest an action in progress right now.
'Will' refers to a future action, not to a daily routine.
The present perfect would connect the action to an unspecified past time.

questions.explanation:
'Every morning' indica una accion habitual y por eso pide el presente simple. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.statement: What does 'usually' tell us in the sentence: 'I usually walk to school'?

options.feedback: 'Once' describes frequency, but 'usually' is the opposite of 'once'.
'Never' is the opposite of 'usually'.
'Usually' is a frequency adverb, not a time marker.

options.text: It happens often but not always.
options.feedback: 'Usually' marks a high frequency without being absolute.

questions.explanation:
'Usually' indica que la accion ocurre con frecuencia pero no siempre. Conviene practicarlo con otros ejemplos antes del examen.
